=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DjD-h ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:988
Reply-to-id: 3275479884

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep one PIN cell tabbable when no cell is focused**

This roving-tabindex logic makes every cell `tabindex="-1"` whenever `focused_index` is `None`. Because `focused_index` starts as `None` on init and is reset to `None` on blur, the component can end up with no tabbable element at all, so keyboard users cannot tab into the PIN input group. Ensure a fallback cell (typically index 0) gets `tabindex="0"` when no cell is currently focused.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DjD-q ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:523
Reply-to-id: 3275479895

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block Clear mutations when PinInput is readonly**

The readonly guard blocks `InputChar`, `DeleteChar`, and `Paste`, but it does not block `Event::Clear`, even though `Clear` later wipes all cells and resets state. In readonly mode this allows value mutation through a clear action (for example from adapter-level clear/reset wiring), which violates readonly semantics. Include `Event::Clear` in the readonly guard or make the clear branch a no-op when readonly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DjD-s ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:674
Reply-to-id: 3275479900

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Start stepping from finite value when input is empty**

With default props (`min = -∞`, `max = +∞`, `value = None`), stepping uses `unwrap_or(ctx.min)`, so the first increment/decrement on an empty field computes from `-∞` and stores a non-finite value. That propagates into `value`/`aria-valuenow` as `"-inf"` and breaks normal numeric behavior from the default configuration. Use a finite baseline (for example `0.0` when empty) before applying step math.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DjD-v ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/password_input/mod.rs:317
Reply-to-id: 3275479905

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync controlled/context fields on props updates**

This machine snapshots `props.value`/flags into `Context` during `init`, but the impl never overrides `Machine::on_props_changed`, so `Service::set_props` will not emit any sync events for later prop changes. In controlled usage, parent updates (e.g. new `value`, `disabled`, `invalid`) can leave rendered attrs/state stale because `input_attrs` reads from `ctx` rather than current `props`. Add a props-sync path (like `SetValue`/`SetProps`) so context tracks prop updates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DjD-x ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/password_input/mod.rs:657
Reply-to-id: 3275479907

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make description linkage reachable at runtime**

The `aria-describedby` helper depends on `ctx.has_description`, but this context flag is initialized to `false` and there is no event/props-sync path in this machine that can ever set it to `true`. As a result, rendering a Description part will not be reflected in `aria-describedby` for real usage, so assistive tech misses help text unless adapters patch attrs manually.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
```

> AGENT

5 legitimate findings, all P1/P2. Plan:

| # | Component | Severity | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PinInput | P1 | Roving tabindex strands keyboard users when `focused_index == None` | Default cell 0 to `tabindex="0"` when nothing focused |
| 2 | NumberInput | P1 | Stepping from empty value with default `min=-∞` produces `-inf` | Use finite baseline (`0.0` clamped) when value is `None` |
| 3 | PasswordInput | P1 | No `on_props_changed`/`SetProps`/`SetValue` — controlled mode broken | Add the standard sync events + impl |
| 4 | PinInput | P2 | `Event::Clear` not guarded by readonly | Add `Clear` to readonly guard |
| 5 | PasswordInput | P2 | `Context::has_description` initialized to `false` with no event to flip it | Add `Event::SetHasDescription(bool)` |

Finding #3/#5 are actually the same defect class (missing prop-sync events) and the same defect exists in SearchInput / NumberInput / PinInput too — Codex only flagged PasswordInput but the no-deferral rule says fix all four. Starting with PasswordInput.

  "new_string": "fn stepped_plan(ctx: &Context, step: f64, up: bool) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let current = ctx.value.get().copied().unwrap_or_else(|| baseline(ctx));\n    let raw = if up { current + step } else { current - step };\n    let next = round_to_precision(clamp(raw, ctx.min, ctx.max), ctx.precision);\n\n    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n        ctx.value.set(Some(next));\n    }))\n}\n\n/// Returns the finite baseline used when stepping/scrubbing from an empty\n/// value. Always finite — `0.0` if it falls inside `[min, max]`, otherwise\n/// the nearest finite bound, defaulting to `0.0` when both bounds are\n/// non-finite (the default `min = -∞`, `max = +∞` config).\nfn baseline(ctx: &Context) -> f64 {\n    if ctx.min.is_finite() && ctx.max.is_finite() {\n        clamp(0.0, ctx.min, ctx.max)\n    } else if ctx.min.is_finite() && ctx.min > 0.0 {\n        ctx.min\n    } else if ctx.max.is_finite() && ctx.max < 0.0 {\n        ctx.max\n    } else {\n        0.0\n    }\n}"

  "new_string": "        // Roving tabindex: the focused cell is the tab stop. When no cell\n        // is focused (the initial / post-blur state), fall back to the first\n        // cell so the group remains tabbable from the document — without this\n        // fallback, every cell carries `tabindex=\"-1\"` and keyboard users\n        // cannot enter the PinInput at all.\n        let is_focused_cell = self.ctx.focused_index == Some(index);\n        let is_default_tab_target = self.ctx.focused_index.is_none() && index == 0;\n\n        attrs.set(\n            HtmlAttr::TabIndex,\n            if is_focused_cell || is_default_tab_target {\n                \"0\"\n            } else {\n                \"-1\"\n            },\n        );"
}

{

  "old_string": "**Application Order**: Precision rounding is applied AFTER clamping to min/max but BEFORE storing in Context.",
  "new_string": "**Application Order**: Precision rounding is applied AFTER clamping to min/max but BEFORE storing in Context.\n\n### 1.5.1 Stepping baseline when `value == None`\n\n`Increment` / `Decrement` / `IncrementLarge` / `DecrementLarge` MUST use a **finite baseline** when no current value is set:\n\n1. If `[min, max]` contains `0.0`, the baseline is `0.0`.\n2. Otherwise the baseline is the nearer finite bound (positive `min`, or negative `max`).\n3. With the default props (`min = f64::NEG_INFINITY`, `max = f64::INFINITY`), the baseline is `0.0`.\n\nThis prevents `unwrap_or(min)` from producing `-∞` when the field is empty under the default configuration, which would propagate non-finite values into `ctx.value` and `aria-valuenow`."
}
```

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync controlled PIN value when length changes**

When `Event::SetProps` handles a `length` change, it only resizes `ctx.value` via `set(...)` and never updates the controlled slot with `sync_controlled(...)`. In controlled mode, `ctx.value.get()` still returns the old vector, so shrinking `length` can leave stale extra digits in outputs like `hidden_input_attrs()` (which joins `ctx.value.get()`), causing submitted form data to diverge from the rendered cells. Resize updates should also synchronize the controlled value path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel debounce effect when CancelDebounce is sent**

`Event::CancelDebounce` is documented as cancelling any active debounce timer, but this branch returns `None` and emits no `cancel_effect`, so a previously scheduled `Effect::SearchDebounce` remains active. In flows that explicitly send `CancelDebounce` (for example adapter lifecycle cleanup or manual cancellation), the timer can still fire later and produce stale behavior. This event should return a transition plan that cancels `Effect::SearchDebounce`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp focused index when PIN length shrinks**

When `length` is reduced via props while focus is on a removed cell index, `SetProps` resizes `value` and `length` but leaves `focused_index` unchanged. That stale out-of-range index makes the roving-tabindex logic mark every rendered cell as `tabindex="-1"` (no index matches, and fallback-to-first does not apply because `focused_index` is not `None`), so keyboard users can no longer tab back into the control.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restart debounce when debounce prop changes**

A debounce prop change currently only updates context flags in `SetProps`; it never cancels/restarts an already pending `SearchDebounce` effect. If a timer is active and `debounce` is updated, the old timer continues with the stale duration, so subsequent debounced behavior does not reflect current props until the next `Change` event. Prop-sync should explicitly cancel and reschedule the debounce effect when this prop changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-finite parsed values from Change**

`Event::Change` accepts any `f64` parse result and stores it directly, which includes non-finite values such as `NaN` or infinity. With the current text-based input attrs, users (or programmatic input events) can produce these strings, leading to invalid `ctx.value` and non-numeric `aria-valuenow` output. Guarding with `value.is_finite()` (and ignoring/rejecting non-finite parses) keeps the machine’s numeric contract intact.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use native required attribute on PasswordInput input**

The component sets only `aria-required` when `required=true`, but omits the native `required` attribute on the actual `<input type="password">`. In forms relying on browser constraint validation, this means the field is announced as required to assistive tech but is not actually blocked from empty submission. Add `HtmlAttr::Required` so required semantics work at submit time.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use native required attribute on NumberInput input**

Like PasswordInput, NumberInput only writes `aria-required` and never sets the native `required` attribute on the form-participating input element. This creates a mismatch where AT announces required state but native form validation will still allow empty submission. The required prop should also set `HtmlAttr::Required` on the input.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove required from hidden PIN field and validate visible cells**

The `required` prop is applied to `HiddenInput` (`type="hidden"`), but hidden inputs are barred from native constraint validation, so this does not enforce required PIN entry at form submit time. As implemented, `required=true` can silently fail to block empty submissions. Required enforcement should be attached to visible, user-editable inputs (or custom validation), not the hidden field.

  "old_string": "    #[test]\n    fn pin_input_set_props_resizes_value_when_length_changes() {\n        let mut svc = service(props().length(4));\n\n        drop(svc.set_props(props().length(6)));\n\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().length, 6);\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().value.get().len(), 6);\n    }",
  "new_string": "    #[test]\n    fn pin_input_set_props_resizes_value_when_length_changes() {\n        let mut svc = service(props().length(4));\n\n        drop(svc.set_props(props().length(6)));\n\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().length, 6);\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().value.get().len(), 6);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pin_input_set_props_shrinks_controlled_value_through_controlled_slot() {\n        let mut svc = service(\n            props()\n                .length(4)\n                .value(vec![\"1\".into(), \"2\".into(), \"3\".into(), \"4\".into()]),\n        );\n\n        assert!(svc.context().value.is_controlled());\n\n        // Shrink the length. Without syncing the controlled slot,\n        // `get()` would still return the 4-cell vector and the hidden\n        // input would join \"1234\" instead of \"12\".\n        drop(svc.set_props(\n            props()\n                .length(2)\n                .value(vec![\"1\".into(), \"2\".into(), \"3\".into(), \"4\".into()]),\n        ));\n\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().length, 2);\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().value.get().len(), 2);\n\n        let api = svc.connect(&|_| {});\n        assert_eq!(api.hidden_input_attrs().get(&HtmlAttr::Value), Some(\"12\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn pin_input_set_props_clears_focused_index_when_out_of_range() {\n        let mut svc = service(props().length(4));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Focus {\n            index: 3,\n            is_keyboard: false,\n        }));\n\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().focused_index, Some(3));\n\n        drop(svc.set_props(props().length(2)));\n\n        // index 3 is now out of bounds; SetProps must clear it so the\n        // roving tabindex falls back to cell 0 (otherwise every cell is\n        // -1 and the group is unreachable).\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().focused_index, None);\n\n        let api = svc.connect(&|_| {});\n        assert_eq!(api.input_attrs(0).get(&HtmlAttr::TabIndex), Some(\"0\"));\n        assert_eq!(api.input_attrs(1).get(&HtmlAttr::TabIndex), Some(\"-1\"));\n    }"
}

We only want\n        // to verify the cancel event was emitted by on_props_changed.\n        let result = svc.set_props(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(500)));\n\n        assert_eq!(result.cancel_effects, alloc::vec![Effect::SearchDebounce]);\n    }"

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DkScO ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:673
Reply-to-id: 3275914542

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Transition to focused state after deleting a filled PIN cell**

When `DeleteChar` runs on a non-empty cell, this branch only mutates context and leaves the FSM state unchanged. If the current state is `Completed`, deleting one digit flips `ctx.complete` to `false` but keeps `State::Completed`, so `data-ars-state` and any completed-state behavior remain incorrect until another transition (for example blur) happens. This is user-visible whenever a completed PIN is edited in place.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DkScR ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/search_input/mod.rs:540
Reply-to-id: 3275914546

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restart debounce timer when debounce prop changes**

On `debounce` prop updates, the machine only emits `CancelDebounce`; it never schedules a new debounce effect for the current input value. If a user has typed (timer active) and the app adjusts debounce settings before expiry, the pending search is dropped permanently unless another `Change` event occurs. That loses expected search propagation for the current text and contradicts the documented debounce-prop-change behavior in this component spec.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DkScT ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:817
Reply-to-id: 3275914549

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute PIN state when controlled value changes completeness**

`SetValue` updates `ctx.complete` but is implemented as a context-only plan, so it never transitions out of `State::Completed` when the incoming controlled value becomes incomplete (for example parent syncs from `"1234"` to `"12"`). In that case the machine reports `complete = false` while still exposing completed state, which desynchronizes `data-ars-state` and downstream behavior driven by state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DkScY ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:566
Reply-to-id: 3275914554

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply precision rounding when jumping directly to bounds**

`IncrementToMax` stores `ctx.max` directly without passing through the component’s clamp+round path. With `precision` configured and a bound like `max = 1.005`, triggering Home/End-style bound jumps can persist unrounded values (for example `1.005` instead of `1.01`), while every other mutation path applies round-half-up. This makes value semantics inconsistent across interaction modes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DkSce ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:852
Reply-to-id: 3275914560

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exit focused state when length shrink invalidates focus index**

When `SetProps` reduces `length` and the old focused cell falls out of range, this code clears `ctx.focused_index` but does not transition state. The machine can therefore remain in `State::Focused` with no focused cell, which makes `data-ars-state` inconsistent and leaves focus-dependent behavior operating on contradictory state/context after dynamic length changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DkSch ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:541
Reply-to-id: 3275914566

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear scrubbing marker when blur ends interaction**

The `Blur` transition always moves to `State::Idle` but never resets `ctx.scrubbing`. If blur occurs during an active scrub gesture (for example pointer capture loss or focus transfer), context can report `scrubbing = true` while state is idle, causing stale interaction flags and inconsistent behavior for adapters that read context to render drag/scrub affordances.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "old_string": "    #[test]\n    fn search_input_debounce_prop_change_cancels_active_timer() {\n        let mut svc = service(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(200)));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Change(\"r\".to_string())));\n\n        // Service::set_props delivers events one at a time. We only want\n        // to verify the cancel event was emitted by on_props_changed.\n        let result = svc.set_props(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(500)));\n\n        assert_eq!(result.cancel_effects, alloc::vec![Effect::SearchDebounce]);\n    }",
  "new_string": "    #[test]\n    fn search_input_debounce_prop_change_cancels_and_restarts_timer() {\n        // Spec §1.5: prop change must CANCEL and RESCHEDULE so the\n        // in-flight search adopts the new duration instead of being\n        // silently dropped.\n        let mut svc = service(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(200)));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Change(\"r\".to_string())));\n\n        let result = svc.set_props(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(500)));\n\n        // Cancel the old timer\n        assert_eq!(result.cancel_effects, alloc::vec![Effect::SearchDebounce]);\n        // AND schedule a fresh one with the new duration\n        assert_eq!(result.pending_effects.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(\n            result.pending_effects[0].name,\n            Effect::SearchDebounce\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn search_input_debounce_prop_change_to_none_only_cancels() {\n        // If the new `debounce` is None, debouncing is disabled —\n        // cancel without rescheduling.\n        let mut svc = service(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(200)));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Change(\"r\".to_string())));\n\n        let result = svc.set_props(props().no_debounce());\n\n        assert_eq!(result.cancel_effects, alloc::vec![Effect::SearchDebounce]);\n        assert!(result.pending_effects.is_empty());\n    }"
}

Without round_to_precision\n        // applied, ctx.value would be 1.5; with round_half_up at 0 decimals\n        // it becomes 2.0 — proving the rounding path is wired through.\n        let mut svc = service(props().min(0.0).max(1.5).precision(0));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::IncrementToMax));\n\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().value.get(), &Some(2.0));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_decrement_to_min_rounds_to_precision() {\n        // `-1.5` is exactly representable. === PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1WY ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:779
Reply-to-id: 3276113452

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp rounded spinbutton values back into range**

Rounding after clamping can push the stored value outside `[min, max]` (for example, `max = 1.5` with `precision = 0` produces `2.0`), so `aria-valuenow` can exceed `aria-valuemax` and boundary logic no longer reflects the configured range. This affects normal step events through `stepped_plan`, not just edge cases, and should be fixed by ensuring the final stored value is clamped after rounding (or by using a bounded rounding routine).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1Wd ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/search_input/mod.rs:505
Reply-to-id: 3276113460

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restart debounce only when a timer is active**

`Event::RestartDebounce` always schedules a new `SearchDebounce` effect whenever `debounce` prop changes to `Some`, even if no debounce timer is currently in flight. That means a plain prop update can create a fresh debounce expiration without a preceding `Change` event, which can trigger unsolicited search-side effects in adapters that fire callbacks on debounce expiry.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1Wf ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/password_input/mod.rs:600
Reply-to-id: 3276113463

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve typed password when toggling visibility**

The input is always rendered with `value` from `ctx.value`, but there is no user-input change event path in this machine to keep `ctx.value` in sync while typing. In uncontrolled usage, a user can type a password and then lose it on the next rerender-triggering action (for example clicking the visibility toggle), because the old context value is written back into the DOM.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1Wh ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:1310
Reply-to-id: 3276113467

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect RTL when mapping arrow-key cell navigation**

The key mapping helper hard-codes `ArrowLeft -> FocusPrev` and `ArrowRight -> FocusNext`, which inverts expected visual movement for RTL layouts. The spec for this component calls out RTL behavior, so adapters using this helper will navigate PIN cells in the wrong direction for RTL users.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1Wi ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:1225
Reply-to-id: 3276113470

**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove ARIA attribute from hidden input element**

The hidden form input is already non-exposed by virtue of `type="hidden"`; adding `aria-hidden` to it is invalid markup for this element type and can fail strict HTML/a11y validation gates. Since the hidden semantics are intrinsic, this ARIA attribute should be dropped rather than emitted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1Wn ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/search_input/mod.rs:773
Reply-to-id: 3276113475

**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable clear trigger when readonly blocks clear action**

The clear button is only marked disabled when `disabled=true`, but `Event::Clear` is explicitly ignored for `readonly=true`. This leaves an apparently interactive control that always no-ops in readonly mode, which is confusing for users and assistive tech; the trigger should be disabled whenever clear is not actionable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1Wo ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/search_input/mod.rs:392
Reply-to-id: 3276113479

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep searching state while loading after refocus**

When `loading` is already true, a subsequent focus event forces the machine into `State::Focused`, which makes state-driven UI (for example a loading indicator shown only in `Searching`) disappear even though a search is still in flight. This creates contradictory output (`loading=true` but non-searching state) and should preserve `Searching` while loading remains true.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dk1Wr ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:1311
Reply-to-id: 3276113482

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle Delete separately from Backspace in PIN keydown**

The keydown mapping treats `Delete` and `Backspace` identically, but `Delete` should clear the current cell rather than trigger backspace-style previous-cell behavior when the current cell is empty. As written, pressing Delete on an empty non-first cell can erase the previous digit, which is an unexpected destructive action for Delete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "old_string": "const fn clamp(value: f64, min: f64, max: f64) -> f64 {\n    let lower = if value > min { value } else { min };\n\n    if lower < max { lower } else { max }\n}",
  "new_string": "const fn clamp(value: f64, min: f64, max: f64) -> f64 {\n    let lower = if value > min { value } else { min };\n\n    if lower < max { lower } else { max }\n}\n\n/// Combined clamp + round-half-up pipeline used by every value-mutating\n/// transition. Order matters and **must terminate with a clamp**: rounding\n/// can push a bound-value across the bound itself (e.g. `max = 1.5` under\n/// `precision = 0` rounds up to `2.0`, which would otherwise leave\n/// `aria-valuenow > aria-valuemax`), so the final clamp pulls the value\n/// back into `[min, max]`.\nfn round_and_clamp(value: f64, min: f64, max: f64, precision: Option<u32>) -> f64 {\n    clamp(\n        round_to_precision(clamp(value, min, max), precision),\n        min,\n        max,\n    )\n}"
}

The clamp pulls it back.\n        let mut svc = service(props().min(-1.5).max(0.0).precision(0));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::DecrementToMin));\n\n        let value = svc.context().value.get().expect(\"value set\");\n        assert!(value >= -1.5, \"stored value {value} must not undercut min\");\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().value.get(), &Some(-1.5));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_stepped_plan_clamps_after_rounding() {\n        // Step from below the max, then verify rounding never pushes\n        // ctx.value past the configured bound.\n        let mut svc = service(props().min(0.0).max(1.5).step(0.5).precision(0));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Increment));\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Increment));\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Increment));\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Increment));\n\n        let value = svc.context().value.get().expect(\"value set\");\n        assert!(value <= 1.5, \"stepped value {value} must respect max\");\n    }"

  "new_string": "    #[test]\n    fn search_input_debounce_prop_change_skips_restart_when_no_timer_active() {\n        // RestartDebounce must NOT schedule a fresh timer when no\n        // `Change` has scheduled one yet — otherwise a plain prop tweak\n        // would fabricate an unsolicited `DebounceExpired` against an\n        // unchanged value.\n        let mut svc = service(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(200)));\n\n        // No `Change` sent, so no timer is in flight.\n        assert!(!svc.context().debounce_pending);\n\n        let result = svc.set_props(props().debounce(Duration::from_millis(500)));\n\n        assert!(result.pending_effects.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn search_input_focus_during_loading_preserves_searching_state() {\n        // When a search is in flight (loading=true) and the user clicks\n        // back into the input, state must stay `Searching` — switching\n        // to `Focused` would clear `data-ars-state=\"searching\"` and any\n        // loading-indicator wiring keyed on state.\n        let mut svc = service(props());\n\n Added `round_and_clamp(value, min, max, precision)` helper that\n  does `clamp → round → clamp` and routed every value-mutation site\n  (stepped_plan, IncrementToMax, DecrementToMin, SetValue, Scrub, Blur)\n  through it. Final clamp pulls bound-exceeding rounded values back into\n  range.\n\nP1 — PasswordInput missing Change event\n  The machine had no path to capture user typing in uncontrolled mode,\n  so any rerender-triggering event (visibility toggle being the obvious\n  one) would write the stale init-time `ctx.value` back to the DOM and\n  erase the typed password. Added `Event::Change(String)` with the same\n  disabled/readonly guard pattern as TextField, plus `Api::on_input_change`\n  for adapter wiring.\n\nP2 — SearchInput RestartDebounce should not fire without an active timer\n  Round 3's RestartDebounce always scheduled a fresh `SearchDebounce`\n  effect on any `debounce` prop change, even when no `Change` had ever\n  started one. Added `ctx.debounce_pending: bool` tracked by Change (set\n  true), DebounceExpired/CancelDebounce/Clear/Submit (all set false), and\n  used by RestartDebounce to skip the reschedule when `!was_pending`.\n\nP2 — PinInput on_cell_keydown must respect RTL\n  ArrowLeft/ArrowRight were hard-mapped to FocusPrev/FocusNext, inverting\n  visual movement for Hebrew/Arabic users. Added `dir: Direction` to\n  PinInput Props/Context (with builder + SetProps sync) and reversed the\n  arrow mapping when `ctx.dir == Rtl`.\n\nP2 — PinInput Delete must not delete the previous cell\n  Backspace and Delete were both mapped to `Event::DeleteChar`, so Delete\n  on an empty non-first cell would erase cell N-1 (Backspace semantics).\n  Added `Event::ClearCell { index }` for Delete: clears the current cell\n  if non-empty, no-op otherwise, never navigates. Backspace continues to\n  use DeleteChar.\n\nP2 — SearchInput Focus during loading must preserve Searching state\n  Focus arm always targeted `State::Focused`, so refocusing during an\n  active search dropped `data-ars-state=\"searching\"`. Now targets\n  `Searching` when `ctx.loading` and `Focused` otherwise.\n\nP3 — SearchInput ClearTrigger disabled when readonly\n  The transition arm ignores `Event::Clear` in readonly mode, but the\n  trigger only rendered `disabled` when `disabled=true`. Now also\n  disabled when `readonly=true` so the visual affordance matches the\n  no-op behaviour.\n\nP3 — PinInput hidden input must not set aria-hidden\n  `<input type=\"hidden\">` is already non-exposed to AT by virtue of its\n  element type; `aria-hidden` on it is invalid markup. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp value after min/max props change**

When `SetProps` updates `ctx.min`/`ctx.max`, the existing `ctx.value` is left untouched, so a value that was previously valid can become out-of-range after a prop update. In that case `input_attrs()` will emit an `aria-valuenow` outside the new `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`, and increment/decrement boundary behavior is computed from a stale value until another user event happens. Clamp/round the current value during `SetProps` when bounds or precision change to keep the spinbutton contract valid immediately after prop updates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
```

  "old_string": "            Event::SetProps => {\n                let props = props.clone();\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    ctx.min = props.min;\n                    ctx.max = props.max;\n                    ctx.step = props.step;\n                    ctx.large_step = props.large_step;\n                    ctx.precision = props.precision;\n                    ctx.disabled = props.disabled;\n                    ctx.readonly = props.readonly;\n                    ctx.invalid = props.invalid;\n                    ctx.required = props.required;\n                    ctx.name = props.name.clone();\n                    ctx.spin_on_press = props.spin_on_press;\n                }))\n            }",
  "new_string": "            Event::SetProps => {\n                let props = props.clone();\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    let bounds_or_precision_changed = (ctx.min - props.min).abs() > f64::EPSILON\n                        || (ctx.max - props.max).abs() > f64::EPSILON\n                        || ctx.precision != props.precision;\n\n                    ctx.min = props.min;\n                    ctx.max = props.max;\n                    ctx.step = props.step;\n                    ctx.large_step = props.large_step;\n                    ctx.precision = props.precision;\n                    ctx.disabled = props.disabled;\n                    ctx.readonly = props.readonly;\n                    ctx.invalid = props.invalid;\n                    ctx.required = props.required;\n                    ctx.name = props.name.clone();\n                    ctx.spin_on_press = props.spin_on_press;\n\n                    // Reclamp + reround the current value when the bounds\n                    // or precision change. Without this, `aria-valuenow`\n                    // can fall outside `[aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax]`\n                    // and boundary checks for Increment/Decrement keep\n                    // computing from a stale value until a user event.\n                    if bounds_or_precision_changed && let Some(value) = *ctx.value.get() {\n                        let was_controlled = ctx.value.is_controlled();\n                        let bounded = round_and_clamp(value, ctx.min, ctx.max, ctx.precision);\n                        ctx.value.set(Some(bounded));\n                        if was_controlled {\n                            ctx.value.sync_controlled(Some(Some(bounded)));\n                        }\n                    }\n                }))\n            }"
}

The\n  check is gated by `bounds_or_precision_changed` so harmless prop\n  updates (e.g. renaming, toggling required) don't silently mutate\n  value.\n\nTests (4 new):\n* `*_set_props_clamps_value_when_max_shrinks_below_current`\n* `*_set_props_clamps_value_when_min_rises_above_current`\n* `*_set_props_rerounds_value_when_precision_tightens`\n* `*_set_props_skips_reclamp_when_bounds_unchanged`\n  (asserts the negative case — only a name change must not mutate value)\n\ncargo xci-fast: all 10 gates green. 1988 unit + 51 proptest + 19\nspec_conformance + 16 doctest tests pass.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3 && git push 2>&1 | tail -3",

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept Unicode digits in numeric PinInput mode**

`Mode::Numeric` currently checks `is_ascii_digit()`, so non-ASCII decimal digits (for example Arabic-Indic numerals entered from localized keyboards or pasted OTP codes) are rejected as invalid input. In those locales, valid one-time codes can never fill the cells, so completion and submit flows fail despite user input being semantically numeric.

> AGENT

Single P2 finding. `Mode::Numeric` uses `is_ascii_digit()` but the spec says "Unicode digit category". `char::to_digit(10).is_some()` is the right test — it accepts ASCII 0-9, Arabic-Indic ٠-٩, Devanagari ०-९, etc. without overreaching to Roman numerals or fractions.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DmkPv ===

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp typed values before exposing spinbutton aria-valuenow**

`Event::Change` writes parsed input directly into `ctx.value` without clamping/rounding, but `input_attrs()` always mirrors `ctx.value` into `aria-valuenow` while also emitting `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`. When a user types an out-of-range number (for example `999` with `max=100`), the component exposes an invalid spinbutton range to assistive tech until blur, which can trigger accessibility validator failures and incorrect announcements. Consider clamping for ARIA-facing state (or omitting `aria-valuenow` while the raw edit is out of range).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DmkPx ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:879
Reply-to-id: 3276742681

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve controlled value when length/value props change together**

When `value` and `length` props change in the same `set_props` cycle, `on_props_changed` emits `SetValue` before `SetProps`, and `SetValue` resizes the incoming controlled value using the *old* `ctx.length`. That can truncate newly provided digits (e.g., 4→6 with a 6-cell value), and `SetProps` then syncs this already-truncated vector, so the machine loses parent-provided data. `SetValue` needs to use the new length (or run after `SetProps`) to avoid destructive updates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DmkP0 ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:1103
Reply-to-id: 3276742686

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return false when number keydown is dropped by transition**

`on_input_keydown` returns `true` for Arrow/Page/Home/End unconditionally after dispatching, even when the state machine ignores that event (for example in `readonly`/`disabled` mode where transition returns `None`). That violates this method’s own “handled by the core machine” contract and can make adapters suppress native key behavior based on a false positive handled result.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DmkP2 ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/pin_input/mod.rs:1418
Reply-to-id: 3276742690

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return false when readonly pin key events are ignored**

`on_cell_keydown` always returns `true` for Backspace/Delete after dispatching, but the machine drops those events when `readonly` is set. In that mode the key is not actually handled, so returning `true` can cause adapters to prevent native behavior or skip fallback logic even though no state change occurred.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    /// Handles normalized keydown data on the input element.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` when the key was handled by the core machine.\n    /// In `disabled` / `readonly` modes the transition arms drop these\n    /// events, so the method also returns `false` there — otherwise\n    /// adapters would suppress native key behavior on a false positive.\n    pub fn on_input_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData) -> bool {\n        if data.is_composing {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Arrow / Page / Home / End all hit the disabled-or-readonly\n        // guard in `transition` — short-circuit here so the return\n        // value reflects what the machine actually does.\n        if self.ctx.disabled || self.ctx.readonly {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        let event = match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => Event::Increment,\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => Event::Decrement,\n            KeyboardKey::PageUp => Event::IncrementLarge,\n            KeyboardKey::PageDown => Event::DecrementLarge,\n            KeyboardKey::Home => Event::DecrementToMin,\n            KeyboardKey::End => Event::IncrementToMax,\n            _ => return false,\n        };\n\n        (self.send)(event);\n\n        true\n    }"
}

  "old_string": "    /// Handles normalized keydown data on a single cell.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` when the key was handled by the core machine.\n    pub fn on_cell_keydown(&self, index: usize, data: &KeyboardEventData) -> bool {\n        if data.is_composing {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // RTL reverses the visual direction of arrow-key navigation:\n        // ArrowRight should move toward earlier cells (visually left),\n        // ArrowLeft toward later cells (visually right). Without this,\n        // Hebrew/Arabic users get inverted navigation.\n        let is_rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;\n\n        let event = match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {\n                if is_rtl {\n                    Event::FocusNext\n                } else {\n                    Event::FocusPrev\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => {\n                if is_rtl {\n                    Event::FocusPrev\n                } else {\n                    Event::FocusNext\n                }\n            }\n            // Backspace = clear current OR navigate-to-prev on empty cell.\n            // Delete = clear current cell only, never navigate (so Delete\n            // on an empty non-first cell is a no-op instead of erasing\n            // the previous digit).\n            KeyboardKey::Backspace => Event::DeleteChar { index },\n            KeyboardKey::Delete => Event::ClearCell { index },\n            _ => return false,\n        };\n\n        (self.send)(event);\n\n        true\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "    /// Handles normalized keydown data on a single cell.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` when the key was handled by the core machine.\n    /// In `disabled` / `readonly` modes the destructive events\n    /// (`Backspace`, `Delete`) are dropped by the machine — so the\n    /// method also returns `false` for those keys in those modes,\n    /// otherwise adapters would suppress native key behavior on a\n    /// false positive.\n    pub fn on_cell_keydown(&self, index: usize, data: &KeyboardEventData) -> bool {\n        if data.is_composing {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // RTL reverses the visual direction of arrow-key navigation:\n        // ArrowRight should move toward earlier cells (visually left),\n        // ArrowLeft toward later cells (visually right). Without this,\n        // Hebrew/Arabic users get inverted navigation.\n        let is_rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;\n\n        let event = match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {\n                if is_rtl {\n                    Event::FocusNext\n                } else {\n                    Event::FocusPrev\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => {\n                if is_rtl {\n                    Event::FocusPrev\n                } else {\n                    Event::FocusNext\n                }\n            }\n            // Backspace = clear current OR navigate-to-prev on empty cell.\n            // Delete = clear current cell only, never navigate (so Delete\n            // on an empty non-first cell is a no-op instead of erasing\n            // the previous digit). Both go through the disabled/readonly\n            // guard in `transition`, so report `false` here when the\n            // machine would drop them.\n            KeyboardKey::Backspace => {\n                if self.ctx.disabled || self.props.readonly {\n                    return false;\n                }\n                Event::DeleteChar { index }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Delete => {\n                if self.ctx.disabled || self.props.readonly {\n                    return false;\n                }\n                Event::ClearCell { index }\n            }\n            _ => return false,\n        };\n\n        (self.send)(event);\n\n        true\n    }\n}"
}

The visible `value`\n        // attribute keeps the raw text so mid-typing edits are visible,\n        // but `aria-valuenow` is bounded.\n        let mut svc = service(bounded_props().default_value(50.0));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::Change(\"999\".to_string())));\n\n        let api = svc.connect(&|_| {});\n        let attrs = api.input_attrs();\n\n        assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Value), Some(\"999\"));\n        assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueNow)), Some(\"100\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_keydown_returns_false_when_disabled() {\n        let svc = service(bounded_props().disabled(true));\n        let api = svc.connect(&|_| {});\n\n        for key in [\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp,\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown,\n            KeyboardKey::PageUp,\n            KeyboardKey::PageDown,\n            KeyboardKey::Home,\n            KeyboardKey::End,\n        ] {\n            let data = keyboard_event(key, false);\n            assert!(\n                !api.on_input_keydown(&data),\n                \"disabled machine must not claim {key:?} as handled\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_keydown_returns_false_when_readonly() {\n        let svc = service(bounded_props().readonly(true));\n        let api = svc.connect(&|_| {});\n\n        for key in [KeyboardKey::ArrowUp, KeyboardKey::Home] {\n            let data = keyboard_event(key, false);\n            assert!(!api.on_input_keydown(&data));\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_change_rejects_non_finite_values() {"

{
  "command": "git add -A && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nfix(input): address Codex review #657 round 7 findings\n\nFour findings from Codex's seventh pass on #657: 1 P1, 3 P2.\n\nP1 — PinInput on_props_changed event order corrupts simultaneous\nlength+value updates\n  When `length` and `value` props both change in one `set_props` cycle,\n  `on_props_changed` previously emitted SetValue before SetProps.\n  SetValue's resize closure captures `ctx.length` at transition() time,\n  so a 4→6 length change with a fresh 6-cell value would truncate the\n  6-cell value down to 4 cells against the OLD length, and SetProps\n  would then lock in the truncated vector — destructive against\n  parent-provided data.\n\n  Fix: reordered on_props_changed to emit SetProps first, then\n  SetValue. SetProps updates ctx.length first so SetValue's\n  transition() captures the NEW length. New test\n  `pin_input_set_props_with_simultaneous_length_and_value_preserves_full_value`\n  guards against the regression by setting length=4 → 6 and value to a\n  6-cell vector in one call, then asserting cells 4 and 5 carry the\n  fresh values.\n\nP2 — NumberInput aria-valuenow exposes out-of-range values during\ntyping\n  `Event::Change` writes raw parsed input into `ctx.value`, and\n  `input_attrs` mirrored that straight into `aria-valuenow`. Adapters that suppress native key behavior on\n  `handled=true` would do so on a false positive.\n\n  Fix: short-circuit return `false` when `ctx.disabled || ctx.readonly`\n  before dispatching. Arrow keys still return true (they are not\n  guarded). **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow scrub termination after disabling number input**

When a `NumberInput` is already in `State::Scrubbing`, this disabled/readonly guard also rejects `Event::EndScrub`. If the parent flips `disabled` or `readonly` during an active drag (e.g., while submitting), the adapter will still emit `EndScrub` on pointer-up, but the machine ignores it and can remain stuck with `data-ars-state="scrubbing"`/`ctx.scrubbing=true` until some unrelated blur/reset occurs. `EndScrub` should remain processable (or `SetProps` should force-clear scrubbing) so the state can always exit cleanly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DnMmy ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:705
Reply-to-id: 3276972204

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve controlled source of truth on bounds updates**

In controlled mode, `SetProps` currently overwrites the controlled slot with a clamped value when `min`/`max`/`precision` change. That lets the machine diverge from `props.value`: for example, if the parent keeps `value=75` while tightening `max` to `50`, the component mutates itself to `50`, and later renders with the same `value=75` won’t emit `SyncValue` (because the prop is unchanged), so the control stays desynchronized from the parent. Controlled inputs should not self-author new controlled values here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard Home/End jumps when bounds are unbounded**

Avoid setting the value to `±inf` in `IncrementToMax`/`DecrementToMin` when `max`/`min` are unbounded. With default props (`min = -∞`, `max = +∞` at lines 261–262), sending `Event::IncrementToMax` or `Event::DecrementToMin` stores a non-finite value, and `input_attrs()` later serializes it into `value`/`aria-valuenow` (`"inf"`/`"-inf"`), which breaks the numeric spinbutton contract and can surface invalid values to assistive tech and form consumers. These events should no-op (or clamp to a finite fallback) when the corresponding bound is not finite.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DnnyZ ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:674
Reply-to-id: 3277124859

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-finite controlled values in SyncValue**

`Event::Change` explicitly rejects `NaN`/`±Inf`, but `Event::SyncValue` accepts any `f64` from controlled props and writes it directly into state. If a parent computes and passes a non-finite value, the component emits invalid textual values (`"NaN"`/`"inf"`) through the input while ARIA is clamped separately, creating inconsistent output and violating the same spinbutton invariants this module enforces for user-entered values. `SyncValue` should apply the same finite check (and clamp/round path) as other value setters.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Dnnyb ===
Path: crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs:774
Reply-to-id: 3277124862

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp precision before casting it to i32 for powi**

`precision` is a public `Option<u32>`, but rounding converts it with `p as i32` before calling `powi`. Large values can wrap/sign-flip during the cast or produce `inf` factors, which then drive `(value * factor ...)/factor` into non-finite math and collapse results to bounds unexpectedly. This makes valid API inputs produce incorrect numeric updates; cap precision to a safe exponent range (or handle overflow explicitly) before `powi`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/ericson/.t3/worktrees/ars-ui/t3code-e1654fe1/crates/ars-components/src/input/number_input/mod.rs",
  "old_string": "/// Round-half-up: ties move away from zero.\n///\n/// Banker's rounding (`f64::round_ties_even`) is unsuitable for interactive UI\n/// because end users expect `2.5` to round to `3` rather than `2`. See\n/// `spec/components/input/number-input.md` §1.5 for the rationale.\nfn round_to_precision(value: f64, precision: Option<u32>) -> f64 {\n    let Some(p) = precision else {\n        return value;\n    };\n\n    let factor = 10_f64.powi(p as i32);\n\n    (value * factor + 0.5_f64.copysign(value)).trunc() / factor\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Maximum precision honoured by [`round_to_precision`]. Caps at the f64\n/// significant-digit budget (~15–17 decimal digits); higher precisions\n/// cannot be represented anyway, and crucially this cap also prevents\n/// the `as i32` cast below from wrapping for arbitrary `u32` inputs and\n/// keeps `10.0_f64.powi(p)` finite (`powi(p > 308)` saturates to `+inf`,\n/// which would collapse the rounding math).\nconst MAX_PRECISION: u32 = 15;\n\n/// Round-half-up: ties move away from zero.\n///\n/// Banker's rounding (`f64::round_ties_even`) is unsuitable for interactive UI\n/// because end users expect `2.5` to round to `3` rather than `2`. See\n/// `spec/components/input/number-input.md` §1.5 for the rationale.\nfn round_to_precision(value: f64, precision: Option<u32>) -> f64 {\n    let Some(p) = precision else {\n        return value;\n    };\n\n    // Cap precision before casting to i32: large `u32` values would\n    // wrap negative through `as i32`, and `10.0_f64.powi(p)` saturates\n    // to `+inf` for any `p > 308`. Both cases poison the rounding math.\n    let p = p.min(MAX_PRECISION);\n\n    let factor = 10_f64.powi(p as i32);\n\n    (value * factor + 0.5_f64.copysign(value)).trunc() / factor\n}"
}

NaN/Inf\n        // would serialize as `\"NaN\"`/`\"inf\"` into the visible input\n        // attribute — same defect class `Change` already guards against.\n        let mut svc = service(bounded_props().value(10.0));\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().value.get(), &Some(10.0));\n\n        for bad in [f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY] {\n            drop(svc.send(Event::SyncValue(Some(bad))));\n            assert_eq!(\n                svc.context().value.get(),\n                &Some(10.0),\n                \"non-finite {bad:?} must be rejected\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_sync_value_accepts_finite_value_and_drops_none() {\n        let mut svc = service(bounded_props().value(10.0));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::SyncValue(Some(42.0))));\n        assert_eq!(svc.context().value.get(), &Some(42.0));\n        assert!(svc.context().value.is_controlled());\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::SyncValue(None)));\n        assert!(!svc.context().value.is_controlled());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_precision_caps_at_max_precision() {\n        // Without capping, `precision = u32::MAX` would wrap to a\n        // negative `i32` and `10.0_f64.powi(neg)` would produce a\n        // tiny fraction, scrambling the rounding math. Verify the\n        // cap clamps to MAX_PRECISION (~15 decimals).\n        let mut svc = service(bounded_props().precision(u32::MAX).default_value(0.0));\n\n        drop(svc.send(Event::SetValue(1.5)));\n\n        // Should still produce a finite, sensible result close to 1.5\n        // (1.5 itself if precision is capped where it can preserve\n        // the value, or a small rounding artefact).\n        let value = svc.context().value.get().expect(\"value set\");\n        assert!(value.is_finite(), \"value {value} must be finite\");\n        assert!((value - 1.5).abs() < 1.0, \"value {value} must be near 1.5\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn number_input_set_props_preserves_controlled_value_when_bounds_shrink() {"
}
